subject: Banking
title: Lender of Last Resort
description: Learn Lender of Last Resort in one minute.

hook.text: Walter Bagehot wrote the rule in 1873: in a crisis, lend freely, at a high rate, against good collateral.

buildup.text: When banks panic, everyone tries to withdraw at once. Only a central bank has unlimited capacity to provide cash.

discovery.text: The lender of last resort stops bank runs by guaranteeing liquidity. If people know cash is available, the panic stops.

twist.text: The safety net creates moral hazard. Banks take bigger risks knowing the central bank will rescue them if it goes wrong.

climax.text: Every central bank bailout prevents a crisis but encourages the next one. Safety nets enable risk-taking.

punchline.text: Lend freely in a crisis. But the safety net invites more risk.

quiz.question: What is moral hazard in banking?
options: Banks take more risk knowing they'll be rescued

details.summary: The lender of last resort concept, formalized after the 1866 Overend Gurney crisis, holds that central banks must lend freely during panics to prevent solvent banks from failing due to temporary liquidity problems.
details.whyItMatters: Without a lender of last resort, every liquidity crunch could become a solvency crisis. This function is the single most important reason central banks exist, preventing panics from becoming depressions.
takeaways: Walter Bagehot described the principle: lend freely at a penalty rate against good collateral
The concept was developed after the 1866 financial crisis in London
Modern applications include the Fed's emergency lending during 2008 and 2023

faq.question: What is Bagehot's rule for lending in a crisis?
faq.answer: Walter Bagehot wrote in 1873 that the central bank should lend freely to any solvent institution, at a penalty rate higher than normal, against good collateral. This stops panic while punishing those who need the help.

faq.question: Has the lender of last resort role expanded beyond Bagehot's vision?
faq.answer: Significantly. During 2008 and 2020, central banks lent to investment banks, bought corporate bonds, and provided liquidity to non-bank financial institutions. Bagehot's principle has been stretched far beyond its original scope of helping solvent commercial banks.
